annotations.keyFindings: Sets out the assumptions of the design and the biases from broad case definitions, late specimens, repeat tests and poor calendar-time adjustment.

Of 112 studies from 2010 to 2018, 38 restricted testing to a clinical case definition, 44 percent adjusted for calendar time finer than monthly, 61 percent reported specimen timing and 27 percent measured prior-season vaccination.
annotations.limitations: Studies to 2018 only; reporting rather than practice.

annotations.keyFindings: Repeat tests biased estimates towards the null by up to 8 percentage points; restricting to the first test per patient per season removed most of that bias.
Of 46 studies since 2021, 29 excluded SARS-CoV-2-positive patients from controls, 11 kept them and 6 did not report the choice.
annotations.limitations: Few sensitivity analyses reported by the included studies.

annotations.keyFindings: Among 2,860 patients tested both ways, 21 percent of rapid-antigen-negative patients were PCR-positive; rapid results alone lowered estimates by 9 percentage points in a simulation.
Self-report agreed with the register for 86 percent of 1,530 older adults; estimates differed by 5 percentage points with the source used.
annotations.limitations: Older adults only; pharmacy vaccinations sometimes missing from the register.

annotations.keyFindings: Care home residents are often excluded or not reported separately; outbreak testing breaks a key assumption of the design.
Including specimens taken more than 7 days after onset lowered estimates by 12 percentage points; restricting to within 4 days gave the most stable estimates.
annotations.limitations: Timing missing for 9 percent of specimens.

synthesis: Eight retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Methods overviews and a survey of 112 studies show that test-negative studies vary widely in case definition, calendar-time adjustment, specimen timing and prior vaccination, and often do not report these choices. Simulations and pooled analyses show that repeat tests, late specimens and rapid antigen testing each move estimates by several percentage points. Since 2021 studies have handled SARS-CoV-2-positive controls inconsistently. Care home residents are rarely reported separately. The evidence supports mapping methods choices rather than pooling estimates.
gradeRationale: Methods overviews, simulations and observational or meta-research studies; consistent in showing variation but indirect for any single choice.
summary: Eight retrieved records appraised; five claims; overall certainty low.
